result.title: Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding for Temporally Grounded Audio-Visual Understanding
result.summary: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) are designed to represent the temporal structure of audio and video, yet it remains unclear how effectively they use this temporal information to relate sounds to visual events. To examine this, we probe an AV-LLM on an audio-visual synchronization task by shifting the audio so that the queried sound overlaps a different visual event. We observe that the model still favors the originally aligned event over the newly aligned one, indicating limited sensitivity to changes in audio-visual temporal alignment. To address this, we propose Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding (MSCD), a training-free decoding method that emphasizes audio-visual temporal alignment in model predictions. MSCD contrasts logits under preserved and disrupted temporal alignment to favor predictions supported by aligned audio and video. We disrupt this alignment by temporally shifting either the audio or the video, while keeping the other modality fixed. Extensive evaluations with two AV-LLMs across three benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of MSCD for temporally grounded audio-visual understanding. In particular, MSCD improves accuracy over the base models on Daily-Omni by 2.2 and 2.8 percentage points for OmniVinci and video-SALMONN 2+, respectively, suggesting that emphasizing temporal alignment can also benefit broader audio-visual understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 论文通过时间平移音频、制造音视频事件错位，检验 AV-LLM 是否真正依据跨模态时间对齐作答，并提出免训练对比解码 MSCD，对比对齐与破坏对齐时的 logits 以强化时间一致的预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接触及多模态推理是否使用时间证据与模态对齐信息，而非依赖表面捷径；其对齐扰动与解码期证据筛选思路可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据使用和贡献分配问题。
